val run [options]

Start an eval run of an existing suite, or upload a versioned suite file and run
it. The upload-and-launch h

as a 120s deadline overall, not per request (raise it
with the global --timeout <ms>); --wait-timeout bounds the RUN instead.
Options:\n --suite <id-or-name> Eval suite name or ID\n --file <path> Versioned
suite file to upload and run (.yaml or .json, or - for stdin)\n --project <id-or-name> Project name or ID (de
faults to the most recently updated project)\n --server <id-or-name...> Override the suite's saved server select
ion (HTTP servers only)\n --environment <id-or-name...> Attached project environment(s) to run. Several values start
one PAID RUN each.\n --client <id-or-name...> Attached client(s) to run, so the run is stamped with that client'
s config. Several values start one PAID RUN each.\n --host <id-or-name...> Deprecated alias for --client. NOT
the host-compat catalog id `mcpjam tools --host` takes.\n --all-targets Run EVERY attached environmen
t (or, if none, every attached host) — one PAID RUN per target\n --iterations <n> Run each case this man
y times under verdict policy 2 (1-10)\n --repetitions <n> Legacy spelling of --iterations\n --case <id-o
r-title...> Run only these cases instead of the whole suite\n --exclude-skills Run the
'without skills' arm: no skills are pinned, and the run is labelled as excluded\n --refresh-snapshot PERS
ISTS a new host-config snapshot on the suite, changing every future run of it. Single-target runs only.\n --notes <text>
Free-text note stored on the run\n --min-pass-rate <n> Pass threshold for this run (0-10
0)\n --match-options <json> Tool-call match options for this run, e.g. '{\"toolCallOrder\":\"exact\"}'\n --id
empotency-key <key> Retry key for a lost launch response; for --file, one is minted and printed when omitted\n
--wait Wait for every started run to reach a terminal status\n --wait-timeout <ms>
Maximum time to wait for completion (default 600000; a run held for its judge gets up to 31 more minutes unless this fl
ag is set)\n --reporter <json-summary|junit-xml|html> Render the completed run report to stdout\n --out <path>
Atomically write the completed report selected by --reporter (default: json-summary)\n --compose-client <id-or-name>
Compose a stack to run instead of naming a saved environment: the client it runs as. Default is EPHEMERAL (does not a
ttach to the suite).\n --compose-host <id-or-name> Deprecated alias for --compose-client\n --compose-computer <id-
or-name> Sandbox image to pin on the composed stack\n --compose-model <id...> Model(s) to run on the

ole saved model selection (source, connection, settings.reasoningEffort) as JSON (or @file, or -): one cell for its model, at its
effort. Alongside --compose-model. Repeat it to add several selections for one model (e.g. at low and at high) — each distinct sel
ection is its own cell.\n --with-client-default Also launch an inherit cell that uses each client's pinned mo
